findings.claim: The fetch stub's jsonResponse returns a plain object with only ok, status and json(); it has no text(), headers or statusText, unlike a real fetch Response. TASK 4 asks sendJson to return null for a 204 and to attach the parsed body (or null if unparseable) on errors, which naturally invites the common, correct pattern of reading response.text() and JSON.parse-ing a non-empty body. Repro: in a scratch copy of the reference solution, changing only sendJson to parse via response.text() (success and error paths) makes t4, t5, t6 and t7 fail (4 failed | 4 passed); the TypeError 'response.text is not a function' is caught by the form and shown as the network-failure banner, so the learner sees a misleading 'Could not reach the server' instead of a stub limitation. The 204 json()-rejects fidelity itself is correct (a sendJson that always calls json() fails t6/t7 with an unhandled SyntaxError).
findings.recommendation: Build stub responses with the platform Response (available in the Vitest jsdom environment, as Headers already is): new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }). That keeps 204 json() rejecting while supporting text(), headers.get() and clone(), so every valid learner parsing strategy passes.

findings.claim: The final block ('Fixing the fields clears the errors on the next submit') is vacuous: after a valid submit the form calls onSave, the stub POST succeeds and RegisterServicePage navigates to '/', unmounting the form, so queryByText('Enter a service name.') is absent whether or not the learner ever clears fieldErrors. Repro: in a scratch copy of the reference solution, changing handleSubmit to set fieldErrors only when client validation fails (never clearing stale errors) still passes all 7 public tests (only the overlay's own learner test catches it). Such a solution leaves a stale 'Enter a service name.' error and aria-invalid='true' on a now-valid field during the in-flight request and after any server/network failure, contradicting TASK 3's 'set aria-invalid on the field exactly while it has an error'.
findings.recommendation: Keep the form mounted for the re-validation check: e.g. set api.holdNextMutation = true (or api.failNetwork = true) before the second submit, then assert the name/team errors are gone and the fields no longer have aria-invalid='true'; or fix only the name, submit, and assert the name error is gone while the team error remains and no request was sent.

findings.claim: TASK 8 step 5 tells learners to 'assert with findBy that the error disappears'. findBy* waits for an element to appear and rejects if it never appears; it cannot assert disappearance (the parenthetical then says queryBy proves absence, contradicting the instruction). This is wrong teaching against the ui-tests topic objective o2 (getBy present, queryBy absent, findBy appears asynchronously), which the topic page teaches correctly. Step 3's rationale ('it renders after a state update, so pick the right query variant') also implies getBy would fail, although after an awaited user-event click the synchronous state update is already flushed inside act, so getBy works there; findBy is safe but not required.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite step 5 as: after the second awaited click, assert absence with expect(screen.queryByText('Enter a service name.')).not.toBeInTheDocument() (or waitForElementToBeRemoved / waitFor for asynchronous removal), and assert onSave was called with the values (inside waitFor if needed). Reword step 3 to say findBy is the safe choice when the element may appear asynchronously, without implying getBy cannot work after an awaited user-event call.

findings.claim: Troubleshooting says 'Task 4's test hangs - make sure handleSubmit awaits onSave inside try/finally so the button re-enables even on failure.' Repro: in a scratch copy of the reference solution with the finally removed (button stays disabled with 'Saving...' after a failure), t4 passes and nothing hangs; t5 fails fast with 'Unable to find an accessible element with the role "button" and name "Save service"'. The symptom and the test named are both wrong, so a learner will not match this advice to the failure they see.
findings.recommendation: Re-target the entry: 'Task 5 cannot find the Save service button after a server error - the button is still disabled/labelled Saving...; reset the pending state in a finally block so it re-enables on failure.'

findings.claim: The node prerequisite '>=22.12' (and README 'Node.js 22.12 or newer') admits Node 23.x, but the committed tests lockfile records vitest 4.1.12 with engines.node '^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0' (react-router 7.18.5 requires >=20, vite 6.4.6 '^18 || ^20 || >=22'), so Node 23 is outside the test runner's declared support range.
findings.recommendation: Declare the node prerequisite as '^22.12.0 || >=24' (and say 'Node.js 22.12+ (LTS) or 24+' in the README), matching the strictest engines range in the lockfiles.
